Editing attention alone, dense/shared projections alone, or routed experts alone removes only 0.039, 0.016, and 0.148 of refusal, respectively. Editing all three together removes 0.776. In other words, roughly three quarters of the removable effect appears only under joint editing, not within any single module family. That directly argues against a simple picture in which refusal is localized to one component type. First, the authors recover the prior direction. Given the unembedding matrix W and an empirical unigram distribution p_unigram, they solve a linear least-squares problem over the frequent-token subset to find a vector d_prior such that softmax(W d_prior) reconstructs the unigram distribution as closely as possible. This requires only the output weights and token counts from a corpus, with no model forward passes. They argue that the recovered direction is unique under the fitting procedure and show that it is absent at random initialization but emerges through training. Second, they derive a tempered Bayesian interpretation. For any final prediction state y_pred, they decompose it into λ d_prior plus an orthogonal component. Plugging this into the softmax yields a factorization of the predictive distribution into a unigram prior raised to the power λ times a context-dependent likelihood term. This gives λ a clean probabilistic meaning: λ=0 removes the prior, 0<λ<1 tempers it, λ>1 sharpens it, and λ<0 inverts it. Third, they validate the mechanism dynamically and causally. They vary contextual informativeness through coherent context, shuffled tokens, short contexts, and ambiguous prompts, and track λ. They also intervene directly on the prediction state along d_prior and compare against norm-matched random-direction perturbations to test whether this axis is functionally special.99:T59b,The experiments cover Llama, Qwen, Gemma, and Pythia, from 0.4B to 405B parameters. Four results matter most. First, existence and universality: a single direction reconstructs the unigram prior with low KL error across all tested families, suggesting this is not an artifact of one architecture or recipe. The paper also shows that the direction is not present at initialization and appears only after training. Second, context dynamics: λ decreases as coherent information accumulates, but not merely when token count grows. Shuffled or semantically weak contexts do not reduce λ in the same way, which supports the claim that λ tracks information rather than length or position. Third, causal intervention: increasing the projection along d_prior pushes predictions toward the unigram prior, while decreasing it makes predictions rely more on contextual evidence. Random directions with matched magnitude do not produce the same effect, so d_prior is not just a post hoc statistical fit. Fourth, scaling behavior: the paper reports that in the high-context regime, λ often decreases with hidden dimension across families, hinting that larger models suppress default priors more effectively when context is informative. The technical contribution has two main parts.

First, it separates the static and dynamic descriptions. In the high-dimensional limit d→∞, the population loss is shown to depend on only finitely many trace-type order parameters, even though the original parameter space is Θ(d^2). So the loss landscape admits a finite-dimensional macroscopic description. However, online SGD is richer: for both tied and untied factorizations, the updates generate an infinite hierarchy of joint matrix moments, and no fixed finite set closes the dynamics in general. The authors then prove that the empirical trajectory converges to a deterministic infinite-dimensional ODE, and that finite-order truncations approximate this limiting dynamics with exponentially decaying error. This is the key methodological result.

Second, the paper analyzes parameterization-induced implicit bias by comparing three representations of the same effective attention: direct optimization of S, tied factorization S=WW^T, and untied factorization S=UV^T. Direct optimization suffers from an information-exponent bottleneck: when first-order correlation vanishes, SGD can remain trapped in an uninformative phase on the d^2 log d sample scale. In the tied case, the PSD structure provides an automatic symmetry-breaking mechanism. Under a mild non-degeneracy condition, this enables weak recovery at Θ(d^2 log d) samples. In the untied case, the mechanism is different: there is a fast-slow decomposition. Quantities such as 1/sqrt(d) Tr(UV^T) evolve on a fast timescale and create a boundary layer; the slower matrix-moment dynamics then proceed from the state selected by that fast transient. Weak recovery occurs only if this early shift breaks the relevant symmetry.9d:T5e8,The empirical component is mainly numerical validation of the theory rather than large-scale model benchmarking. The important results are threefold.

First, the paper shows that finite-order truncations of the infinite moment hierarchy provide accurate approximations, with error decreasing rapidly as the truncation order increases. This supports the practical tractability of the otherwise infinite-dimensional ODE description.

Second, it compares the three parameterizations under uninformative initialization. Direct optimization of S remains bottlenecked when first-order correlation is absent. The tied PSD factorization achieves weak recovery on the Θ(d^2 log d) sample scale. The untied factorization can either recover or remain uninformative, depending on which symmetry branch is selected during the fast boundary-layer dynamics. The important takeaway is the difference in phase behavior and sample complexity, not a single benchmark number.

Third, numerical trajectories match the theoretical ODE predictions, indicating that the high-dimensional limit is not merely formal. The paper also highlights a sharp distinction from finite-rank sequence-indexed models, where a finite set of order parameters often closes the dynamics; here it does not.

The provided full-text excerpt does not include the complete tables or all numerical settings, so it would be unsafe to quote more exact numbers. The most useful figures are likely the phase diagrams, trajectory plots, and truncation-error curves.9e:T463,For a skim, focus on three things.

It is trying to give a single probabilistic lens for several procedures that are usually discussed separately: few-shot ICL, SFT, KL-regularized RL, on-policy distillation, and test-time search / chain-of-thought. The central claim is that they can all be written in the same two-step pattern: first construct a generalized Bayes or Gibbs posterior from a prior/reference policy plus a utility signal; then fit a parametric model or policy to approximate that posterior or its posterior predictive. The paper focuses on two key identifications. First, under a hierarchical task distribution, few-shot ICL targets the Bayes posterior predictive. Second, SFT is a forward-KL projection onto a teacher conditional distribution, while KL-regularized RL and OPD approximate reward- or advantage-reweighted posteriors under a reference policy. The framework is meant to explain why ICL and SFT can partially substitute for each other, why few-shot prompting can behave oddly on RL-tuned reasoning models, and why OPD, RLHF/RLVR, and search-based inference are less disjoint than they appear.a6:T436,Its value for pretraining research is conceptual rather than algorithmic. It gives a cleaner interface between pretraining, post-training, and test-time adaptation by forcing three questions: what is the target distribution, what role does the prior/reference model play, and whether training and inference-time search are approximating the same posterior or optimizing different objects. For pretraining researchers, two points matter. First, ICL is framed not as a prompting trick but as amortized Bayesian inference learned during pretraining; that changes how one thinks about task mixtures, context structure, and data organization. Second, the differences among SFT, OPD, and KL-regularized RL become easier to localize: KL direction, posterior temperature, utility definition, and approximation family. That helps explain why some post-training signals preserve the pretraining distribution while others overwrite it more aggressively. The contribution is moderate in scale and mostly about unification, but it is useful for thinking about the pretrain↔post-train loop.a7:T806,The paper is a theory-oriented note. Part I starts from standard SFT and rewrites conditional maximum likelihood as a forward-KL projection onto the true teacher conditional q_true(y|x): minimizing expected negative log-likelihood is equivalent to minimizing E_x[KL(q_true(.|x) || p_theta(.|x))] up to an entropy term independent of the model parameters. This matters because it makes SFT explicitly a problem of approximating a target conditional distribution. The paper then introduces a hierarchical Bayesian task model: sample a task function f, then sample within-task demonstrations D_k and a query. For any in-context predictor M(D_k, x), the Bayes posterior predictive is the unique minimizer of expected log-loss. If a Transformer is pretrained over the same task distribution, then in the infinite-data/infinite-capacity limit its optimal predictor is exactly that posterior predictive. The point is not merely to restate “ICL is Bayes,” but to place ICL and SFT inside the same language of target-distribution approximation.

The later sections extend the same template to KL-regularized RL, OPD, and test-time search. The visible excerpt mainly covers Part I, but the abstract and setup make the intended form clear: q*(y|x) ∝ π_ref(y|x) exp(U(x,y)/β), where U can be log-likelihood, reward, advantage, or a search-induced utility. SFT corresponds to a likelihood-defined target; KL-regularized RL corresponds to a reward-weighted posterior; OPD can be viewed as fitting the student to a teacher-defined posterior on student-generated trajectories; and search / CoT acts like posterior reweighting over latent reasoning paths at inference time. The useful decomposition is not by training stage but by prior, utility, temperature, and approximation family. That decomposition clarifies why reverse-KL style policy matching is often mode-seeking, why forward-KL SFT is more support-covering, and why few-shot demonstrations sometimes behave like extra observations for posterior updating but can also conflict with an RL-shaped policy.a8:T6da,The method has two modules. GUT-Q is the uncertainty quantification component. For a given problem, the model is sampled multiple times to produce multiple reasoning chains. The chains are then merged into a directed acyclic graph by identifying semantically equivalent reasoning steps with an NLI model. Nodes represent step-level semantic states; edges represent possible transitions between steps. This is the key move: instead of scoring each sampled chain independently, the method approximates the latent reasoning space induced by token-level stochasticity.

On top of that graph, the paper defines graph complexity as a combination of two signals. One comes from token-level distribution statistics, intended to capture local uncertainty during generation. The other comes from graph topology, intended to capture how that local uncertainty unfolds into global branching structure. The claim is that this joint quantity is a better estimator of reasoning uncertainty than sequence-only or self-prompting approaches.

GUT-O is the optimization component. Since full graph construction is expensive and not directly usable online during RL, the paper introduces a proxy uncertainty measure and uses its negative value as reward. The design choice is important: optimizing only answer correctness does not explicitly discourage unstable or nonsensical intermediate branches, while optimizing shallow signals such as length or entropy may not align with reasoning quality. GUT-O tries to bias the model toward trajectories that are both lower-uncertainty and still task-effective. This differs from self-consistency or reranking methods, which improve outputs at inference time by sampling more; GUT-O attempts to shift the model distribution itself.a9:T4bc,From the full-text excerpts provided, GUT-Q is evaluated on 4 LLMs and 5 datasets against 45 uncertainty baselines, using selective generation as the downstream testbed and AUROC, AUPRC, and PRR as metrics. The reported result is that GUT-Q performs best overall in this comparison, suggesting that graph-based reasoning-space estimates separate reliable from unreliable generations better than single-sequence statistics or simpler diversity measures. GUT-O is tested across 4 model scales and 5 datasets, with the main finding that RL with the uncertainty proxy reduces reasoning uncertainty and also improves accuracy.

The experimental framing is stronger than a simple correlation study. The paper checks whether the uncertainty score is useful for abstention or selective answering, and then checks whether it can function as an optimization signal. That said, the main caveat is methodological cost and attribution: graph construction depends on repeated sampling plus an external NLI model. The critical question is how much of the gain comes from the graph formulation itself, versus extra sampling budget and the quality of semantic merging. The ablations around these components are therefore central.aa:T4d2,For a skim-level read, start with the overview figure and the formal definition of GUT-Q, then read the reward construction in GUT-O, and finally inspect the main selective-generation table. What to focus on:
1. The exact definition of reasoning uncertainty. The paper is not measuring generic predictive uncertainty; it is measuring instability in branching reasoning trajectories.
2. The graph construction pipeline. Check how step boundaries are defined, how semantic equivalence is decided with NLI, and whether logically distinct steps could be over-merged.
3. The decomposition of graph complexity. Understand what the token-statistics term contributes versus the topology term, and whether they partly measure the same phenomenon.
4. The proxy used in GUT-O. Ask whether it tracks the full graph complexity well enough to be a meaningful RL reward.
5. The ablations. The most informative ones are likely: removing NLI merging, using only topology, using only token statistics, and varying the number of samples.

Linear harm probes are trained to separate harmful from benign prompts, and the strongest decodability appears at the architecture-specific write site rather than in the accumulated residual.

It uses a Procrustes rigid rotation to align one model’s representation space to another’s, allowing only rotation, not reshaping. A refusal direction learned in a transformer is mapped into the target architecture’s space, then removed or gated at the target write site. What transfers across architectures is the refusal direction, not a superior defense recipe.ad:T62d,The method, CLWM, augments a standard latent world model with a contrastive counterfactual objective over action-conditioned futures. The base architecture remains familiar: a recurrent belief encoder summarizes history, stochastic latent dynamics model future evolution, and planning is done by imagined rollouts in latent space. The key change is in the training signal. Instead of only optimizing observation, reward, and continuation prediction, the model is explicitly trained to separate imagined futures when different interventions lead to different control-relevant outcomes.

The central object is an action-conditioned latent summary, Φ(h_t, α), obtained by rolling out a candidate action sequence α from belief state h_t. Positive and negative pairs are defined by intervention outcome rather than pixel similarity. If two interventions are behaviorally different, their latent futures should be pushed apart even when their near-term observations are visually similar. If two trajectories are outcome-equivalent, their latent summaries should align despite nuisance visual variation. The paper highlights hard counterfactual negatives as the critical ingredient: these are exactly the cases where standard predictive objectives tend to collapse distinct futures.

The authors also introduce diagnostics beyond task success: counterfactual separability, intervention-outcome prediction, and model-exploitation rate. These metrics are useful because they can audit inherited representations, including pretrained encoders, without requiring the CLWM objective itself.ae:T463,KPI (Key Path Identification) refines a standard SAE-steering pipeline. Starting from a set of ‘positive’ SAE features correlated with the target behavior (faithfulness), it builds an interaction graph among these features using a small development set. Nodes are candidate positive features; edges represent activation/causal dependencies across layers (and potentially within-layer interactions), motivated by the observation that a strongly steering feature often requires upstream features to activate it. KPI then defines key features via graph structure—high indegree features are treated as bottlenecks/aggregators—and constructs key paths by anchoring on a key layer with strong steering effect and tracing back through preceding layers’ key features. Steering is applied only on features along these key paths, aiming to remove redundant features that dilute the intervention. The paper further connects the intervention to attention dynamics: key-path steering increases attention to context-provided ‘golden answer’ tokens and shows a gradual formation of knowledge-selection behavior across depth.af:T7bf,The method is deliberately simple but well targeted. The authors define two axes. Direct rate (DR) measures how often the model repeats its top answer over 30 samples of the original prompt at temperature 0.6. This captures concentration under one wording. Framed rate (FR) then asks whether that same direct top answer survives 30 matched scenario reframings of the underlying question. Importantly, FR is not the concentration of answers under reframing; it is the reappearance rate of the original direct top answer. That design choice is the core of the paper, because it measures persistence of a specific preference rather than generic consistency. The final bias depth score is π = DR × FR, which is high only when the model is both concentrated under direct prompting and robust to reframing.

The dataset construction is also central. They build 4,442 opinion prompt families, each grounded in a real Olmo-3-7B-SFT training example, and create matched everyday-scenario reframings for each family. Because the task is open-ended generation rather than multiple choice, answer normalization is necessary to merge semantically equivalent outputs and avoid contaminating FR with superficial phrasing variation. The contribution is therefore less about a new model and more about turning a causally meaningful question—does a preference survive paraphrastic and situational variation?—into a scalable evaluation protocol.

The paper then runs this protocol across the full Olmo-3-7B release pipeline: Pretrained → SFT → DPO → RLVR. That allows stage-wise tracking of bias depth. It also adds two attribution analyses: whether the post-SFT top answer matches the pretrained top answer, and whether a biased answer can be traced back to a specific SFT training example. Finally, it tests removability using continued LoRA-SFT and prompt-based debiasing with GEPA, asking whether Deep and Shallow biases differ not just in origin but also in how hard they are to erase.b0:T5c3,There are four results that matter most. First, across four post-SFT models, 35.8% to 77.7% of the 4,442 prompt families look biased under direct prompting, but only about a quarter of those direct biases survive reframing. So most of what a single-prompt protocol would count as bias is shallow. Second, along the full Olmo-3-7B pipeline, most Deep bias is already present at the pretrained stage, whereas Shallow bias keeps increasing through SFT and every later post-training stage. That is the clearest empirical support for the paper’s main interpretation. Third, biases that survive reframing are much more likely to match the pretrained model’s top answer, suggesting inheritance from pretraining rather than creation by SFT alone. At the same time, clean attribution to one specific SFT example works only for a small minority of cases, which argues against a simplistic single-example memorization story and points instead to broader distributional effects. Fourth, debiasing is asymmetric: continued LoRA-SFT reduces Deep bias by only 4.5 percentage points versus 10.3 points for Shallow bias, and GEPA reduces Deep bias by 1.6 points versus 5.8 points for Shallow. Those removability gaps line up with the stage-of-origin analysis.

For a pretraining reader, the main signal is not any one absolute score but the consistency of the whole picture: biases with stronger evidence of pretraining inheritance are more robust to reframing and harder to remove later.b1:T483,This is a skim paper, but a careful skim is worthwhile. The key detail is that FR tracks recurrence of the direct top answer under reframing, not the top answer under each reframed prompt. Without that detail, the paper can look like a generic robustness study, which it is not. Then read the dataset section closely enough to understand how prompt families, scenario reframings, and answer normalization are built; the validity of the Deep/Shallow distinction depends heavily on these choices. In the experiments, prioritize the stage-wise analysis, the pretrained-versus-SFT attribution, and the debiasing section. When looking at figures, focus on whether the same answer persists across checkpoints and how much each debiasing method moves Deep versus Shallow cases.

A solid read takes about 25–35 minutes. Instead of inferring head importance from attention weights or output projection weights, it perturbs head outputs directly and measures the resulting change in the layer representation. This is a better intervention point because a head with small projection weights can still matter if its activation is large, and a head with large weights can be inactive in a given context. After filtering causally redundant heads, the method uses counterfactual Difference-in-Differences to disentangle visual and language information at the head level. The remaining heads are categorized as redundant, visual, language, or synergy heads. A condition may be an MMLU subject in a sycophancy test, a decision-topic and demographic cell in a discrimination evaluation, or an agentic scenario. A prediction method outputs one rate per condition, and performance is scored by correlation and calibration on frozen splits. The paper varies three axes independently: information available to the model, from abstract descriptions to exact items and behavior history; the subject of the prompt, including “you,” a named model, and “capable AI agents in general”; and the question format, either direct rate prediction or forced choice. The crucial design choice is the subject control. If self-directed prompts perform no better than generic-agent prompts, positive correlations cannot be interpreted as privileged self-knowledge. Additional controls include noise ceilings, cross-model consensus, predictions from other models’ measured behavior, other models’ answers about themselves, identity transfer, and re-elicitation after finetuning.b4:T599,The study covers nine public behavioral evaluations, 15 prediction methods, and 12 models from six labs, including frontier models with and without reasoning. Direct self-report has almost no predictive power for the reporting model’s behavior, with r=+0.04. Showing the model its own measured history raises this to +0.19, and showing exact evaluation items raises it to +0.24. However, the same item-informed question about capable AI agents in general reaches +0.28, and other models’ self-reports predict the target model at least as well as the target model’s own answers, with +0.35 versus +0.24 in the reported comparison. Each model’s answers fit other models’ behavior nearly as well as its own; the self-advantage is only +0.02. The paper also estimates how much reliable variance is model-specific: about 0.04 for capability-style evaluations, where models mostly agree on what is hard, and about 0.97 for agentic policy evaluations, where models differ more. Scaling improves predictions about AI assistants in general, but not identification of the model’s own tendencies. Naming the model induces a self-flattering shift: on harmful behaviors, self-reports are about 0.15 lower than generic-agent reports. Finetuning on records of the model’s own behavior helps narrowly on the trained behavior, but it also changes the behavior being predicted and transfers poorly across behaviors or abstraction levels.b5:Ta52,方法核心叫 Speculative Uncertainty, SU。输入是一个大 agent 在最近 k=3 个 step 内生成的 reasoning-action 轨迹窗口，目标是预测当前 step 的 action 在执行前是否会满足一个外部可验证目标 Ω，在文中就是“代码执行不抛异常”。

关键做法有三层。

第一层，是把 speculative decoding 反过来。作者引入一个小型开源 draft model q，对黑盒 agent p 已经生成出的 token 序列做 teacher-forced scoring。也就是给定前缀 (x, y<t)，让 q 输出下一个 token 分布，再去读 agent 实际生成 token yt 在 q 下的概率。这样一次前向就能得到整条轨迹的 token-level 信号，不需要访问 p 的 logits，也不需要重复采样。文中提到至少提取了三类逐 token 信号，摘要截断处能确认其中包括 cross-likelihood 以及 draft 自己的 argmax 与 agent token 的偏差类信息；从方法描述看，核心是利用 q 与 p 在局部条件分布上的一致性/不一致性来近似失败风险。

第二层，是 phase-aware feature extraction。作者观察到 agent 轨迹不是同质 token 流，而是明显分成 reasoning phase 和 action phase。reasoning 段自由度高、熵高、语言噪声大；action 段受工具调用语法、参数格式、代码片段结构约束更强，熵低，但也更直接决定执行是否成功。如果像 HTC 那样把整段 token 概率简单平均，reasoning 段会淹没 action 段中真正与失败相关的信号。SU 因此按 harness 的消息结构把 token 标成 reason/action 两类，分别统计特征，再送入校准器。这个设计不是简单 feature engineering，而是在利用 agent 轨迹的生成机制差异。

第三层，是轻量校准。作者没有训练复杂判别器，而是用线性 calibrator 把 phase-aware 特征映射成“下一步 action 会通过验证”的概率。这样做有两个好处：一是样本效率高，便于跨 agent 迁移；二是输出可直接作为 gate/routing/human intervention 的决策分数。部署时，SU 插在 code generation 和 execution 之间。如果预测失败概率高，就先 veto 当前 action，触发更便宜的 replan，而不是进入 execute-fail-retry 循环。

和已有方法相比，区别主要有三点：一，不需要白盒访问；二，不需要多次采样；三，不把轨迹当作均质序列，而是显式建模 reasoning/action 两阶段。作者还强调 draft model 的训练目标并不敏感，说明这里更重要的是 draft 作为一个通用语言先验和局部一致性探针，而不是某种专门蒸馏出来的精确替身。b6:T991,The method, Speculative Uncertainty (SU), operates on a fixed lookback window of the most recent k=3 agent steps. Each step contains a reasoning span followed by an action span. The target is a calibrated probability that the current action will satisfy a verifiable objective Ω before execution; in the coding setting, Ω is whether execution succeeds without exceptions.

The first ingredient is reverse speculative scoring. A small open-weight draft model q is run in teacher-forcing mode over the black-box agent trajectory produced by model p. For each token, q conditions on the prefix and assigns probability to the token actually emitted by p. This yields token-level cross-likelihood style signals in a single forward pass, without access to p’s internals and without repeated sampling. The method relies on disagreement between q’s local distribution and p’s realized tokens as a proxy for downstream failure risk.

The second ingredient is phase-aware feature extraction. The paper argues that agent trajectories are structurally heterogeneous. Reasoning spans are high-entropy and linguistically noisy; action spans are lower-entropy, more syntax-constrained, and more directly tied to execution success. If one averages token scores over the whole trajectory, as in prior holistic calibration approaches, the action-relevant signal gets diluted by the reasoning phase. SU therefore separates reasoning and action tokens using the harness structure and computes features for each phase independently before calibration.

The third ingredient is a lightweight calibrator. Rather than training a heavy classifier, the paper uses a linear calibration layer to map phase-aware features to a failure likelihood. This keeps the method sample-efficient and easier to transfer across agents. In deployment, SU is inserted as a gate between code generation and execution: if the predicted failure risk is high, the system triggers a cheaper replan instead of entering an execute-fail-retry loop.

Relative to prior work such as trajectory calibration with white-box log-probabilities, the differences are clear: no white-box access, no repeated sampling, and explicit modeling of reasoning versus action phases. The paper also notes that the exact draft-model training objective matters little, which suggests the draft is acting more as a generic language prior and consistency probe than as a tightly matched student of the target agent.b7:T6d2,The evaluation is conducted on two agentic coding benchmarks, explicitly including SWE-Bench Verified and DA-Code, with additional zero-shot transfer to an out-of-distribution benchmark. The deployment policy is a pre-execution veto gate: if SU predicts high failure likelihood, the action is blocked and the agent replans.

The headline deployment result is a reduction of per-call execution error rate by 6 to 8 percentage points, alongside a 14% to 19% reduction in average token cost. This is important because the method is not merely improving a calibration metric; it is reducing the expensive retry loop that dominates practical agent cost.

A central ablation concerns phase awareness. The paper’s main claim is that treating the trajectory as a homogeneous token stream weakens the signal, because the high-entropy reasoning portion overwhelms the action-specific failure cues. The reasoning/action split appears to be one of the main contributors to performance over prior holistic scoring baselines.

Another useful result is that the draft model need not be large or highly specialized. A distilled 4B draft is reported to be sufficient, the training objective of the draft matters little, and a draft-calibrator setup trained on one agent transfers to other agents substantially better than an untrained baseline. That makes the method more plausible as a reusable deployment component rather than a benchmark-specific fit.

The most informative parts of the experimental section are likely not the absolute calibration numbers alone, but the transfer results: across agents, across benchmarks, and across draft-model choices. Those are the tests that determine whether SU is genuinely robust under realistic black-box conditions.b8:T5b5,This is a skim paper. 1) TaskPilot: an online, policy-adaptive task synthesis loop. Training proceeds in iterations: when a checkpoint saturates on validation, it triggers a new synthesis/calibration round, so the task distribution co-evolves with the policy. This differs from offline difficulty filtering over a large static pool.
2) Leaf harness: a simplified Claude-Code-like tool interface designed for compact models. The first is environment reconstruction. Starting from public terminal-agent trajectories, the system replays file operations and restores each file to its pre-edit state, so the resulting workspace starts unsolved. Because trajectories usually reveal only a partial view of the original workspace, replay alone produces incomplete environments. A completion agent then fills in missing files and dependencies while trying not to leak the solution. This design choice is important: it avoids generating environments from scratch, which often hurts realism, and it also avoids requiring access to the original repository, which may be unavailable.

The second part is task expansion. The framework does not only recover the original user intent; it also synthesizes new tasks over the reconstructed environment. Breadth expansion links related environments and creates cross-workspace tasks, such as porting a feature from one project to another or connecting two components. Depth expansion turns a single-round task into a multi-round interaction. After one round is completed, a user agent issues grounded follow-up requests based on the changed workspace, or asks for fixes when a round fails. This yields stateful, evolving tasks rather than static instructions.

The third part is verification and data generation. For each new task, an agent writes a verifier inside the container, and only trajectories whose tests pass are kept. Qwen3.7-Max is then used as a teacher to solve tasks again in these reconstructed environments, and the resulting trajectories are used to train Qwen3.5-27B. The key point is the data-generation paradigm: reconstruct the environment first, then let a stronger model produce fresh, verifiable solutions, instead of treating historical trajectories as final supervision.bb:T476,The reported scale is substantial. From public terminal-agent trajectories, the pipeline produces 37.3k task-sufficient environments, meaning the reconstructed workspaces are complete enough to support execution and verification rather than being partial artifacts.

Using newly generated queries over these environments and teacher rollouts from Qwen3.7-Max, the authors train Qwen3.5-27B and report gains of 11.9 points on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 13.8 points on the multi-round benchmark EvoCode-Bench v2 MT@4. Another important detail is that every synthesized task is paired with a verifier and filtered by test success, so the quality of executable supervision is doing a lot of the work.bc:T782,方法由两部分组成。第一部分是 dynamic per-trajectory rubric。不是为整个任务分布预先写一套固定 rubric，而是先根据任务指令生成初始 criteria，再结合每个 rollout 暴露出来的子目标、失败模式和执行路径，对 rubric 做扩展，最后把同一 group 内多个 rollout 提出的 criteria 合并成共享 rubric 集合。这样做的原因很直接：固定 rubric 往往覆盖不到长轨迹里真实发生的分叉和失败细节，而按轨迹动态生成可以让 judge 评价的是“这条轨迹实际试图完成了什么、卡在了哪里”，不是抽象模板。

第二部分是 distribution of rubric-conditioned advantage。标准 GRPO 对同一 trajectory 的所有 token 使用同一个 advantage；DRACO 改成先让 judge 对 rubric 中每个 criterion 给 verdict，再把 criterion 与轨迹中负责该 criterion 的步骤对齐，然后用一个闭式规则把 criterion-level judgment 分摊成 per-step advantage。论文强调这个分配规则满足若干形式性质，包括总量守恒、符号保持、长度无关等，目的是避免 credit 在长轨迹里被无控制地稀释，或者因为轨迹更长而系统性偏置。这里的关键不是“做 step reward”本身，而是 step reward 不依赖终局 verifier，也不依赖 learned reward model，而是直接从 rubric verdict 推出。

训练上仍然套在 GRPO 框架里：对每个任务采样一组轨迹，judge 对每条轨迹按动态 rubric 打分，再把 rubric verdict 重新分配到步骤，形成替代统一 trajectory advantage 的 step-level advantage。论文还比较了 frontier judge 与 self-judge，说明 judge 质量会直接影响 credit 质量。与已有 process reward 或 step-level RL 方法的差别在于，很多先前方法仍然锚定 gold answer、unit test 或 terminal reward；DRACO 刻意去掉了这些训练时真值依赖。bd:T6ef,DRACO has two main components. The first is dynamic per-trajectory rubric generation. Instead of writing one fixed rubric for the whole task distribution, the judge first proposes criteria from the task instruction, then extends those criteria using what each sampled rollout actually attempted, where it failed, and which subgoals emerged during execution. The criteria proposed from all trajectories in the same GRPO group are merged into a shared rubric set. The motivation is straightforward: fixed rubrics under-specify long trajectories, while rollout-conditioned rubrics can evaluate what the policy concretely did rather than what a generic template expected.

The second component is rubric-conditioned advantage redistribution. Standard GRPO assigns one scalar advantage to every token in a trajectory. DRACO asks the judge to score each rubric criterion, aligns criteria to the steps responsible for them, and then applies a closed-form redistribution rule to produce per-step advantages. The paper emphasizes several formal properties of this rule, including conservation of total push, sign preservation, and length independence. These properties are meant to prevent the usual failure mode where long trajectories dilute credit or where trajectory length itself introduces systematic bias.

Training remains within the GRPO framework: sample a group of trajectories, score them with a frozen judge under the dynamic rubric, and replace uniform trajectory-level advantage with redistributed step-level advantage. A notable design choice is that the method does not rely on a learned reward model and does not anchor step rewards to terminal verifiers or gold answers. That is the main distinction from much of the prior process-reward and step-credit literature.be:T662,The main experiments are on AppWorld. The paper states that this is the first RL training result on AppWorld that never accesses the environment’s ground-truth unit-test signal during training. On AppWorld TN, DRACO reaches 85.3 TGC@1, which is a +15.9 point gain over the untrained policy. It also transfers zero-shot to τ-bench and performs at or above a verifier-trained run under the same budget. The key point is not only the absolute score, but that outcome-blind training remains competitive with verifier-based RL.

The ablations separate the two components: dynamic rubric alone, redistribution alone with a fixed rubric, and the full method. The two parts appear complementary. Dynamic rubrics improve coverage and task adaptation, while redistribution improves signal density and credit precision. The paper also compares against a coarse outcome-reward baseline, showing that a single trajectory-level scalar is much weaker for long-horizon learning.

Another useful experiment replaces the frontier judge with a self-judge. Performance drops, but the method still works, suggesting DRACO is not entirely dependent on an extremely strong external judge. That said, judge quality clearly matters because both rubric generation and criterion verdicts feed directly into the RL signal. The paper also analyzes policy efficiency after training and the reward actually optimized by the policy, which is relevant for checking rubric overfitting or reward hacking. Not all ablation numbers are visible in the provided excerpt, but the experimental structure is centered on signal source, credit granularity, and judge quality.bf:T8b7,The central idea is environment evolution. The paper starts from a multi-turn learning objective, models agent-environment interaction as a Markov process, and then introduces a higher-level decomposition of execution into alternating scenarios and skills. From this view, environment difficulty is decomposed into three factors: scenario novelty, skill rarity, and execution length. Intuitively, an environment becomes harder when it requires the agent to enter less common scenarios, apply rarer skills or skill combinations, and sustain a longer meaningful execution chain.

A key step is to move from model-dependent negative log-likelihood to a policy-independent notion of difficulty under a reference distribution T. This is meant to separate environment difficulty from model weakness. In other words, the authors do not want to define an environment as difficult merely because the current policy fails on it. With this formulation, environment generation no longer needs to depend on on-policy rollouts.

The implementation uses a loop-engineered multi-agent harness that incrementally modifies a seed environment along one of three directions: increasing scenario novelty, increasing skill rarity, or increasing execution length. Each modification must preserve executability, task validity, and the verifier. This produces verified lineages of environments with gradually increasing difficulty. The lineage design matters: instead of generating entirely new environments from scratch, the method performs local, controlled, traceable edits on already verified environments, which makes curriculum construction more manageable. Training then schedules these evolved environments generation by generation so that the policy continues to receive non-saturated learning signals over time.

Compared with co-evolution, the main differences are that the process is off-policy and that difficulty increase is explicit and structured rather than driven by current rollout failures. The trade-off is that the quality of the difficulty definition and the evolution harness becomes central: if those are weak, the system may generate environments that are harder in superficial ways but not actually more learnable or more useful.c0:T612,The paper reports 200-step long-horizon RL experiments on Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, environment evolution improves performance by 14.4 and 18.0 percentage points, respectively. The authors also use Hy4 preview, Claude Opus 5, and GPT-5.6 Sol for rollout-based difficulty estimation, showing that the evolved environments remain challenging across different models rather than being overfit to a single generator or policy.

Another important result is that evolved environments continue to provide useful RL signal even after the seed environments have already been used for SFT. That suggests the method is not merely replaying the original distribution, but is actually pushing the environment family into new difficulty regimes. Compared with agent-environment co-evolution and ensemble baselines, the paper claims that off-policy evolution yields longer-lasting learning signals and slower saturation during training.

From an evaluation standpoint, the paper is trying to validate three things: whether the evolved environments are genuinely harder, whether that hardness generalizes across models, and whether the harder environments translate into downstream benchmark gains. For credibility, the most important details are likely in the validation of lineages, preservation of verifiers, and the separate effects of the three evolution directions. The headline numbers are the final benchmark gains, but the more informative evidence is probably in the difficulty calibration and training-curve persistence analyses.c1:T43e,For a skim read, start with the introduction and preliminaries to understand why the paper rejects on-policy pass rate as the primary definition of difficulty. Instead of explicitly enumerating all possible payloads and injection sites, the paper treats the attack surface as a latent space induced jointly by the environment, the benign user task, and the malicious injection task. To search this space, the attacker is given reconnaissance tools of two kinds: tools for understanding the environment and task context, and tools for understanding candidate injection vectors and their constraints.

The attacker then performs structured reasoning over possible strategies, explores promising subspaces, and uses victim-agent feedback plus environment-state changes to adapt future attempts. A key design choice is explicit strategy management. The paper argues that without tracking explored directions, pruning unproductive branches, and maintaining search state, larger compute budgets lead to redundant exploration and weaker scaling. In that sense, the search harness is what turns prompt injection from one-shot payload generation into an iterative attack process. The study is conducted in a white-box environment setting, which makes the attack surface visible to the attacker and isolates the role of test-time search more cleanly; black-box transfer is left for future work.c3:T451,From the available full text, the experiments are organized to show two main findings rather than to optimize a single benchmark number. This is the central empirical claim and supports the paper’s argument that fixed-budget evaluations can underestimate real-world risk. Second, ablations indicate that explicit strategy management matters: when search tracking and redundancy control are removed, gains from larger budgets degrade because the attacker wastes compute revisiting similar attack directions.

That makes the benchmark closer to executable agent behavior than to text-only jailbreak scoring.c4:T461,RSM-full is an online clustered-memory pipeline with two main design choices:
1) Cosine-gated max-member merge write rule: maintain an L2-normalized centroid μ_m per atom/cluster. A new chunk embedding h merges into an atom if cosine(h, μ_m) ≥ τ OR cosine(h, any member in atom) ≥ τ; otherwise create a new atom. The max-member condition makes merging more permissive than pure centroid thresholding, aiming to reduce fragmentation and mis-clustering under streaming drift.
- τ calibration: per embedding space, set τ ≈ Q0.70 of pairwise cosine similarities using ≤50 unlabeled validation examples.
- Write complexity: O(Md) per chunk.
2) Atom-aware grouped context packer: retrieve top-K atoms, rank members within each atom, and pack retrieved chunks grouped by atom (with headers and temporal ordering) rather than a flat relevance-sorted concatenation. The intent is to preserve local coherence and reduce attention interference from interleaving unrelated snippets.

Higher-rank storage/quantization options are mentioned as deployment paths but are not the core explanatory mechanism in the main text.c5:T852,The method, State-Path Tool Menu, has three components: an encoder, a retriever, and a reranker. Each tool has documentation, required inputs, and produced outputs. A request exposes an initial state s0(q), containing the fields and constraints visible before any tool call. The system must construct an ordered menu of K=32 tools, and the online agent can only use tools from that menu during execution.

The central idea is the state path, a latent pre-execution route from the observable initial state to the desired outcome. Tools on this route are assigned one of four roles: entry tools can run immediately from the initial state, bridge tools create intermediate fields needed later, the target tool resolves the main request, and an optional terminal tool commits or delivers the result. This role decomposition is useful because it separates different notions that relevance-based retrieval conflates: immediate executability, intermediate utility, and final-task alignment.

The encoder learns relation-aware tool representations from the request state, tool schemas, and successful training trajectories. The excerpt explicitly mentions three directional signals: whether a tool can run now, whether it produces fields needed later, and how it depends on other tools in precedence order. So the representation is not just semantic similarity over tool descriptions; it is structured around state compatibility and dependency. The retriever then selects 32 tools that cover complementary path roles rather than simply maximizing top-k relevance. The reranker orders the selected tools so that producers appear before consumers, making the menu easier to execute under the same online loop and call budget.

Training supervision comes from successful trajectories. The retriever is trained with route membership, entry, and path-role targets, while the reranker is trained with slot and pairwise precedence targets. A notable design choice is that the paper keeps the online agent unchanged. The gains are meant to come from better pre-execution menu construction, not from modifying the planner or increasing the budget.c6:T4b9,From the available text, the experiments compare State-Path menus against relevance-based menus under a fixed agent and a fixed 32-tool budget. The reported evaluation dimensions include end-task success, complete-chain coverage, and executable entry. The paper also claims comparisons across tool libraries, evaluators, and executor families, plus paired outcomes and controlled variants to isolate whether the gains come from route coverage and ordering.

The provided excerpt does not include the result tables, exact gains, dataset sizes, or training details, so it would be inappropriate to fabricate numbers. Even so, the experimental design is already informative. The control variables are tight: the online execution loop and call budget remain unchanged. The metrics are also more diagnostic than standard success rate alone, because they measure whether the menu contains a complete chain and whether executable tools appear early enough to be useful. When reading the full paper, the most important checks are whether the gains are larger on long dependency chains, whether the method is more robust in larger tool libraries, and whether reranking adds substantial value beyond retrieval coverage.c7:T416,This is a skim paper. Start with the introduction, especially the receipt and email example, because it makes the failure mode concrete: the final tool is easy to retrieve, but the bridge tools determine whether the route is executable. Then read the first half of the methodology section to understand the state-path abstraction, the four tool roles, and why menu order matters before execution begins. After that, go to the main experimental tables and ablations to see whether the gains come mostly from relation-aware retrieval, path-role coverage, or producer-before-consumer ordering.

A focused read should take about 20 to 30 minutes. If you work on agents, the appendices on visible information at each stage, trajectory supervision, and case studies are worth extra time because they determine how realistic the setup is for real API ecosystems. linear-regression model itself, but the separation between data mixture and data schedule. A fixed fraction of synthetic data in a mixed stream can create a non-vanishing excess-risk floor, while a synthetic-then-real curriculum can remove that floor. This supports a practical intuition in LLM training: synthetic data quality and ratio matter, but the stage at which synthetic data enters the run can matter just as much.","technical_approach":"The analysis compares two protocols for last-iterate one-pass SGD. In mixed training, each update is drawn from either the real source or the synthetic source. In two-stage training, the model is first trained on synthetic data and then updated on real data. The risk bounds decompose ordinary bias and variance from mismatch-induced terms. For mixed training, the mismatch appears as fluctuation from random source switching and persistent drift from the shifted synthetic labeling function. For two-stage training, the synthetic phase mainly contributes a filtered initialization bias that can be washed out by the real-data phase. The paper also develops scaling-law-style bounds under a random sketch model, characterizing when larger models amplify synthetic-induced degradation and when high-quality synthetic data reduces bias.","experiments":"The contribution is theoretical. The main finite-sample upper and lower bounds show strong model collapse for mixed training: with a fixed synthetic-data fraction, the excess risk on the real distribution has a non-vanishing floor under data scaling. The same qualitative behavior is shown for iterate-averaged SGD, so the effect is not just a last-iterate artifact. Two-stage training avoids this floor and can achieve vanishing excess risk. Under the random sketch model, the mixed-training bound is tight in an optimization-saturated regime, and the analysis gives an exact finite-sample condition under which two-stage training strictly improves over real-only training with the same real-data budget and real-stage updates.","reading_guide":"Skim in 30–45 minutes. 的平均风险当成充分结论；如果高风险样本集中在少量记录上，平均指标会低估真实隐私代价。第二，它把“记录可记忆性/可辨识性”从模型侧问题推进到数据侧问题：哪些文本更容易在生成后留下痕迹，和数据分布尾部、独特性、群体结构直接相关。这对预训练数据筛选、去重、长尾控制、敏感样本识别都有启发。第三，它给 release-based 审计提供了更现实的框架。很多已有 MIA 依赖访问生成器或训练过程，不适合真实数据发布场景；这里把攻击者知识分层，并把 proxy evidence 与 calibration 分开，方法上更接近实际部署时能做的审计。贡献量级不是提出新的生成模型，而是把隐私评估从平均视角推进到 subgroup-aware、record-level 达到 0.79–0.83；在 FPR 低于 5% 时，可识别 34–61% 的真实成员。即便攻击者只能看到 release，本身也能识别 39–52% 的真实成员，说明单靠发布样本就可能泄露不少信息。加入 DP 后，平均 AUC 明显下降，但所有测试的 privacy budget 下仍高于随机：AUC 约 0.55–0.65，在 5% FPR 下 TPR 最高仍接近 18%。更关键的是，DP 侧，而不是训练范式本身。","technical_approach":"方法分三步。第一步是构造 chunk-summarization 诊断任务。作者把多个短文本摘要数据集里的文档拼成长上下文，并记录每个原始文档边界。然后要求模型先识别语义 chunk 数量，再为每个 chunk 生成关键词。这个任务不是简单检索某个 span，而是要求模型先做结构划分，再做语义压缩，因此更容易激活负责层级聚合的 head。\n\n第二步是给每个 head 打 summarization score。对有效样本，作者追踪生成关键词 token 对输入中对应源词的注意力，把“输出关键词是否能稳定回指到正确 chunk 内的关键信息”作为 head 的重要性信号。具体上，对每个关键词 token，取其对输入中同词出现位置的最大注意力，再在 chunk 和样本维度上聚合，得到每个 head 的平均 summarization 能力分数。这个设计和常见的 retrieval-style head scoring 不同，它奖励的是从压缩表示回连源内容的能力，而不是局部匹配或高频注意力。\n\n第三步是按分数做 KV 预算分配。作者保留固定的 sink tokens 和最近窗口，因为实际对话里系统提示和最近轮次通常最重要；剩余可压缩区间的预算按各 head 的归一化 summarization score 分配。为了避免极高分 head 吃掉过多预算，又引入了类似 water-filling 的再分配算法，把超额预算回流给其他高价值 head。每个 head 内部再用类似 SnapKV 的 cumulative attention 规则选 token。也就是说，SGD-KV 不是替代 token selection，而是在它之上增加一层更细的 head-level resource allocation。和 DuoAttention 这类二元划分 head 的方法相比，它是连续预算；和 HeadKV、AdaKV 相比，它的 head importance 不是从下游 benchmark 直接拟合，而是来自一个专门设计的 summarization probe。","experiments":"实验覆盖两个模型：Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M 和 28.53，说明在高信息覆盖任务上它能更有效地保留关键历史。作者还在附录里做了几类补充：不同摘要数据集上 summarization head 的泛化、不同类型 head 的分数分布比较、最终预算分配可视化。这些实验支持其核心论点：确实存在一类对长程聚合更关键的 head，而且识别它们后，压缩策略会更稳。","reading_guide":"泛读时建议先看 Figure 1 In NoPE-MLA, attention uses a fixed bilinear form, so part of a token’s future usefulness can be treated as a row-intrinsic property. This is not true in the same way for RoPE, where relative rotation makes the winner set depend on the future query position. Each cache row has 576 dimensions, and the method reads only the 64-dimensional decoupled branch, about 11% of the row. A query-independent score ranks rows; the top-m rows remain in the attended tier, while all other rows are moved exactly, not discarded, into a GPU-resident archive. At each decoding step, a certified trigger can recall archived rows when they may affect the current query. The theoretical argument has three parts. First, under NoPE, cache rows are read through a fixed bilinear form, so a row-intrinsic salience signal can exist. Second, exact merging is generally impossible: reproducing attention for all queries requires retaining the distinct rows, due to the linear independence of exponential characters. Third, archive recall can be controlled by a query-uniform bound, |Δs| ≤ λ||Q||ε. full KV 下真正高价值的 token。若读全文，建议重点看 attention 可视化、query 几何分析、以及 beacon 数量和压缩预算之间的 trade-off。","reading_guide":"这篇适合泛读，但不要只看实验表。建议先看 Introduction 里对 TRT 的定义和 failure case，再看分析部分关于 local/global query The paper’s diagnosis is not merely about compressor capacity. It is about supervision mismatch. Prior soft-compression methods usually distill from an uncompressed RAG teacher, which means the student is trained to imitate a computation pattern developed for reading long discrete token sequences. 是合适的。但方法上有两个点对生成模型研究仍有启发。第一，它把“中途改条件”从粗糙的 condition swap 变成了明确的 counterfactual state transport，这种表述对 diffusion/flow 类生成器的可中断推理很有参考价值。第二，它强调在冻结 backbone 和 sampler 的前提下，只学习一个轻量 corrector 去修正内部状态，这是一种很工程化也很干净的接口设计。对做统一生成模型、交互式多模态生成、或者研究 sampler state controllability 的人，这篇可以提供一个清晰的问题定义和评测协议。对纯 LLM 预训练读者，启发主要停留在“生成过程中的中间状态是否可编辑、可校正、可恢复”这一层。","technical_approach":"方法核心是 ActionSplice，其中的关键操作叫 Counterfactual State Transport，简称 CST。设一个冻结的 action-conditioned world model 用 K 步 sampler 生成一个含 T 帧 latent 的 active chunk。若在第 r 步之后收到新动作，当前内部状态 s_r^- 仍位于旧动作 a^- 诱导的轨迹上。作者定义目标状态 s_r^*：它是保持相同初始状态、已提交历史、solver schedule 以及随机性条件不变时，若采用更新后的控制计划 c^(m)，在同一 solver step r 应该到达的 matched counterfactual state。训练时通过 rollback 构造这种配对状态，但推理时不执行 rollback。模型只训练一个轻量 corrector，输入中断时的旧状态和新控制信息，预测 backbone-native transport representation 上的 masked residual，把 s_r^- 修正到接近 s_r^*，然后从该状态继续剩余 K-r 步采样。作者做了两个变体。CST_R 对整个 active chunk 重定向，适合异步用户动作更新。CST_T 只修改从时间边界 m 开始的后缀，保留前缀不变，相当于在一个 chunk 内实现更细粒度的动作切换。另一个值得注意的点是，作者不强行假设不同 backbone 共享同一潜空间，而是在各自可恢复的内部状态空间里定义 transport：对一个 backbone 用 clean-prediction transport，对另一个用 Euler solver-state transport，因此 corrector 需要按 backbone 单独训练。这种设计比追求统一 latent 更务实。","experiments":"实验结果给得比较具体。相对 direct condition swapping，CST_R 在 minWM–Wan Action2V 上把相对 rollback 的 LPIPS 降低 61.5%，在 HY-WM1.5 上降低 75.9%。CST_T 在两套 backbone 上分别把 suffix LPIPS 降低 56.1% 和 In chunk-autoregressive generation, each chunk is typically conditioned on one action while the sampler runs for multiple solver steps. If a new action arrives before the current chunk finishes sampling, the system faces an awkward trade-off: wait until the next chunk and incur control latency, swap the condition and continue from a state already shaped by the old action, or roll back and replay completed solver evaluations. The authors formalize the desired behavior as same-step counterfactual state matching: given the interrupted intermediate state under the old action, recover the state that would have been reached at the same solver step had the revised action been used, without replaying finished computation.","importance":"This is not a core LLM pretraining paper; it is better viewed as a world-model inference and control paper, so skim is the right level. Still, it contains two ideas that are broadly useful for generative modeling. First, it turns mid-generation control editing into a clean counterfactual transport problem rather than an ad hoc condition swap. That framing is relevant to diffusion and flow-based generators more generally. Second, it uses a lightweight learned corrector while keeping the backbone model and sampler frozen, which is a disciplined systems interface. For readers working on unified generative models, interactive multimodal generation, or controllability of sampler trajectories, the paper offers a well-posed problem statement and a stronger evaluation protocol than typical editing demos. For pure LLM-pretraining readers, the main takeaway is conceptual: intermediate generative states can be treated as editable and correctable objects.","technical_approach":"$35","experiments":"$36","reading_guide":"For a skim read, focus on the problem setup before the video-generation details. However, the softmax path often evaluates shifted-score exponentials in higher precision, forms a temporary probability block, and quantizes it before low-bit $PV$ multiplication. This exp-then-quantize path creates a mismatch between a high-precision probability producer and a low-bit matrix consumer. We propose EFQ-Softmax (Exp-Free Quantization for Softmax)","starred":false,"priority":"p2","reading_tier":"skim","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"2026-09-09T05:04:33Z","category_id":"efficient","cover_url":"/covers/2609_09721.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.LG"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇工作解决的是低比特 shifted attention scores 生成可供低比特 PV 消费的概率操作数，同时保持 FlashAttention 式 online recurrence 的数值稳定和归一化一致性。","importance":"对基座模型研究的价值主要在推理效率而不是预训练方法本身。它针对 attention kernel 的中间概率生成路径做了结构性简化，减少高精度 exp 和临时概率 tile 的开销，这对长上下文 LLM、VLM、视频生成模型都相关。更具体地说，这篇工作说明低比特 attention 的瓶颈已经从 GEMM 逐步转移到 softmax probability path；如果矩阵乘已经足够快，剩下的 elementwise exp、临时存储和再量化就会变成新的热点。这个判断对做高效 serving、kernel co-design、甚至训练时的低精度 attention 研究都有启发。不过它更偏系统/算子层，不直接改变预训练范式。","technical_approach":"核心方法是 EFQ-Softmax，目标是把 shifted scores 直接映射成 block-scaled E2M1 概率操作数，绕过传统 exp-then-quantize 流程。作者强调“Exp-Free”并不是完全消灭所有指数运算，而是去掉当前 score block 上密集的 scale-normalized residual domain；再用单一 affine index rule 生成非负 E2M1 code。最终得到的是由 E2M1 code 加上 block-level E8M0 scale 组成的 MXFP4 probability operand。这个 operand 被同时用于 numerator update 和 denominator To overcome these ","starred":false,"priority":"p3","reading_tier":"skim","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"2026-09-09T16:53:02Z","category_id":"efficient","cover_url":"/covers/2609_10441.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.AI","cs.CL"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇工作处理的是一个很具体、也很现实的问题：当输入上下文远超模型原生窗口时，怎样在不重新训练模型、也不引入串行 memory agent 延迟的前提下，做相对可靠的长文档推理。作者针对的是两类现有路线的共同短板。第一类是直接扩上下文窗口，计算和延迟都很重，而且长上下文下常见 lost-in-the-middle，模型并不真正稳定利用远处证据。第二类是 MemAgent 一类顺序读文档、逐步更新记忆的方案，复杂度虽然线性，但推理路径是严格串行的，吞吐差；同时这类方法常依赖 RL 学记忆策略，容易在训练分布上学到捷径，回答看起来对，实际并没有忠实依赖给定上下文。ConvMem要解决的核心，就是把“长文档压缩+证据汇聚+最终回答”改写成一种可并行、层次化、训练无关的推理流程，并尽量减少顺序记忆链带来的误差累积和分布过拟合。","importance":"对基座研究的意义不在于它提出了新的预训练目标，而在于它给出了一种很清楚的 inference-time 结构化归纳偏置：把冻结 LLM 当作语义卷积核，用树形汇聚替代链式记忆更新。这个想法对长上下文系统设计有两点启发。其一，很多所谓“长上下文能力”问题，不一定要继续押注更长 attention，也可以通过外部层次化读写结构来补。其二，作者明确指出 RL-based memory agent 的一个风险：模型可能借助参数记忆和数据集模式完成回答，而不是忠实读取上下文。这一点对 post-train 与 long-context agent 的接口很重要，因为如果训练信号鼓励的是最终答案而不是证据忠实性，系统很容易学成 benchmark-specific policy。量级上，这篇工作更像一个有工程启发的推理框架，而不是会直接改写预训练范式的结果。对做长上下文 serving、memory scaffold、test-time compute 设计的人有参考价值；对纯 pretrain 处理。随后把这些局部摘要再按层次继续聚合，形成树状结构，直到顶层得到可供最终回答的全局记忆。这样推理深度从顺序 agent 的 O(N) 链式步数，变成近似 O(log N) 的层次深度，代价是每层需要更多并行调用。\n\n作者围绕这个主干加了三个机制。第一是 configurable strides。若 stride S < W，就形成重叠窗口，同一段证据会被多个感受野重复扫描。这样做不是为了卷积意义上的平移不变性，而是为了缓解文本边界截断和单次摘要的随机性。长文档 QA 里证据常跨 chunk 边界，重叠扫描能提高召回。第二是 semantic skip connections。层次摘要会丢细节，尤其是实体、数字、关系链中的局部约束。作者让高置信原始证据绕过中间压缩层，直接传到最终回答阶段，类似残差保真。第三是 multi-kernel convolution。复杂问题先被分解成多个子问题，每个子问题对应一个独立 kernel 或语义通道，分别抽取相关证据，最后再汇总。这相当于显式减少不同推理线索之间的干扰。\n\n从方法定位看，ConvMem不是训练一个新模型，而是一个 prompt-and-orchestrate 框架。它依赖底座 LLM 已有的摘要、证据提取和问答能力。与 MemAgent 的关键区别有三点：一是没有显式可学习 memory policy；二是信息流是树而不是链；三是并行性来自同层 chunk 独立处理，而不是一步一步读完整篇文档。与直接 RAG 也不同，ConvMem不是先检索少量块再回答，而是对全篇做层次化覆盖式扫描，因此更接近“全局压缩推理”而不是“局部召回”。","experiments":"实验主要放在 RULER-HotpotQA 和 RULER-2WikiMultiHopQA 这类长上下文多跳问答设置上，目标是比较训练无关方法与 RL 训练的 memory agent。全文给出的主结论有三层。第一，ConvMem 在 training-free baselines 上有稳定优势，说明层次化并行汇聚比单次摘要、简单 map-reduce 或朴素分块问答更适合多跳证据整合。第二，在 out-of-distribution 评测上，ConvMem 的泛化好于 RL-trained memory agent。作者强调后者在分布内成绩可能更高，但换数据后容易掉得明显，且会出现“答案像是对的，但证据并不来自输入文档”的现象。第三，三个结构组件都有效：重叠 stride 提升证据召回，skip connection 改善细节保留，多 kernel 对复杂问题更有帮助。\n\n从全文可读出的实验重点，不是绝对分数刷新多少，而是对 failure mode 的拆解。作者专门分析了 RL agent 的过拟合：当问题与预训练知识或训练集模式有重合时，agent 可能直接依赖参数记忆生成 plausible answer，而不是沿着 memory state 忠实推理。ConvMem因为不训练 policy，反而少了这类 benchmark-specific shortcut。若精读实验部分，建议重点看：1）ID 与 OOD 的分开汇报；2）不同 stride、是否 overlap 的消融；3）是否加入 skip evidence 的消融；4）单 kernel 与多 kernel The target gap is between two existing families. Enlarged-context models remain expensive at inference and often degrade as context grows. Sequential memory agents such as MemAgent reduce complexity to linear-time streaming, but they introduce a hard serial bottleneck and typically rely on RL to learn memory-update policies. It does not modify the underlying MLLM or the pruning algorithms. The candidate set includes Full, FastV, VisionZip, PruMerge+, and DART. Full-token inference is kept as an explicit option when pruning is predicted to be unsafe. The router uses frozen visual and textual preview encoders, a text-to-vision cross-attention module, and a ratio-conditioned MLP utility predictor. The preview encoders provide low-cost representations. Cross-attention extracts query-conditioned visual evidence. The MLP predicts the utility of each candidate strategy for a given retained-token ratio. advantage。论文的重点结果不是某个 benchmark 上涨了多少点，而是排序相关指标在去除或修正疑似污染项后仍较稳定。若只关心“这个 benchmark 还能不能用于比较模型”，作者给出的答案偏保守乐观：静态 benchmark 的绝对分数需要谨慎，但榜单排序通常比想象中稳。由于给出的全文片段未包含完整结果表和具体数值，我不编造未展示的百分点、相关系数或 Kendall benchmark. It asks a narrower and more consequential one: does contamination actually change leaderboard orderings? The authors recast contamination as a failure of anchor-item invariance. An item becomes easier for some models not because they are more capable, but because they memorized the original form. This lets them separate two effects that are often conflated: absolute score inflation and rank distortion. The practical goal is to estimate contamination without access to training corpora, calibrate the signal against known contamination doses, and determine whether observed contamination is mostly shared across models or differential enough to reorder the leaderboard.","importance":"For pretraining research, the contribution is mainly conceptual and methodological. First, it moves contamination from a data hygiene discussion to a measurement-validity discussion: the real issue is not only whether scores are inflated, but whether model comparisons remain trustworthy. Second, it offers a more precise interpretation of static benchmarks: contamination can raise absolute scores while leaving relative rankings largely intact. 两种对话形态。single-turn 每轮重置上下文，只给历史数据；multi-turn 保留完整会话，让模型显式反思之前的 reasoning。总预算固定 N=120，并按维度给 2d 个初始点，保证不同 batch size 下总 oracle 调用数一致。评价指标用 regret，核心看 simple regret。\n\n离散优化部分，作者选的是 PMO 分子优化基准。这里 LLM 直接在 SMILES 字符串空间里提出候选分子，由确定性 oracle 打分。这个设置天然适合语言模型，因为 SMILES 既是离散序列，又携带局部化学结构语义，模型可以利用预训练中形成的字符串模式、子结构替换和约束遵守能力。也正因为如此，这部分实验不是在测“纯优化器”，而是在测“语言先验 + 搜索策略”的组合能力。\n\n全文最有价值的技术判断，是把 LLM 的优化行为解释为一种表示依赖很强的先验推断过程：在连续数值空间里，模型需要从表格化历史点中恢复几何结构，这不是其训练分布中的强项；而在分子空间里，候选生成更接近语言建模中的局部编辑、模板组合和语义约束满足，因此性能更自然。","experiments":"从已给出的全文内容看，连续实验的统一设置是总预算 N=120，batch size 为 1/2/4，初始点数为 2d，覆盖 2 维到 6 维的经典测试函数，并同时测试原始函数与 disguise 版本。作者报告的主结论不是某个函数上小幅领先，而是整体行为特征：前沿 LLM 在若干数值函数上可以接近经典 Gaussian Process Bayesian Optimization + Expected Improvement 这类强基线，但结果很脆弱，受任务变换、维度和 batch size 明显影响。也就是说，性能不是稳定单调的，换一种坐标表示或提高维度后，优势可能消失。\n\n离散分子优化上，作者的结论更强：在 PMO 的一组 oracle 上，Anthropic 系列 reasoning 模型经常能以远低于专用方法的采样预算取得更好的结果，表现出较高样本效率。摘要和正文片段都强调“frequently beating specialist methods with only a fraction of the oracle sampling budget”，这比单纯最终分数更重要，因为黑盒优化里预算才是核心资源。\n\n模型方面，评测对象是 Anthropic 的 Sonnet 4.6、Opus 4.8、Opus 5，用来观察同一家族 frontier reasoning model 的代际变化。全文片段没有给出完整表格数字，因此不能在这里编造具体均值或胜率；但可以确认作者比较了模型代际、single-turn/multi-turn、batch size、原始/变换函数，以及连续/离散两大任务族，这使得结论不是单点现象，而是有一定结构性的。","reading_guide":"泛读时先抓三处。第一，看实验设计部分里连续函数的 disguise 做“行为体检”。\n\n从全文描述看，作者还额外检查了三个稳定性维度：repeat-run variability、evaluator configuration sensitivity、test-suite reproducibility。前两者尤其重要，因为 LLM judge 往往对 prompt、解码设置、模型版本敏感；如果一个评测器在同一输入上多跑几次结论都不稳，那它即便 benchmark 分数里经常被抹平。比如，词汇类方法通常对表面改写过敏，对 correctness-preserving 变换不够稳；语义类和 LLM-based 方法对同义改写更稳，但可能在某些 correctness-altering reliable early-exit signal for reasoning models. The setup is simple: take a partially generated reasoning trajectory, repeatedly probe it for its current answer, and stop once recent probes agree. The authors ask two stricter questions than prior work: can any such rule be both safe and token-saving, and can one operating point be selected once and reused across models and benchmarks? Their answer is no. The issue is not poor threshold tuning. It is that consensus measures persistence of a probe-elicited answer, not completion of the underlying reasoning process.","importance":"This is not a pretraining paper, but it is relevant to anyone working on reasoning models, test-time compute, or trajectory-level analysis. Third, the paper shows that the bottleneck is the signal, not early exit as a goal. 目标太难，于是把被投影压扁的维度拆开，各自给可验证信号。\n\n从架构上看，这不是改 backbone，而是改训练信号与任务分解。它和已有 spatial RLVR 的区别主要有三点：一是从单一 correctness reward 变成 factorized reward；二是从单帧问答转向多视角/时序场景；三是把几何一致性写进奖励，而不是只让模型在语言空间里自发形成空间链路。代价也很明确：需要构造能支持 XY/Z/T 验证的数据与标注，训练管线更复杂，泛化上仍依赖奖励设计是否覆盖真实空间误差模式。","experiments":"文中最重要的结果是多个空间基准上的提升，摘要里给出了两个代表数字：VSI-Bench 提升 Headroom ranks stored groups by remaining learning value: whether the current policy still has room to move probability mass toward high-advantage responses and away from low-advantage ones. Policy Drift gates groups by compatibility with the current policy, using the generation-time policy as the reference. The minimum replay unit is a full GRPO group, not an individual response, because GRPO’s advantage signal is defined by within-group comparison. The buffer stores immutable group-level reference state: actions, generation-time log probabilities, and response-level advantages. This creates a spurious advantage signal in bounded-answer and outcome-only search settings.","importance":"The result is relevant to RLVR and reasoning post-training. GRPO is often used with binary verifiers, but its advantage magnitude depends on the correct/wrong composition inside a rollout group rather than on the causal quality of the trajectory. In multiple-choice tasks, short-answer math, enumerable subcases, and search agents with many possible paths, some correct rollouts are lucky or low-quality. If these rollouts receive high imitation weight, the policy can learn answer priors or search detours instead of robust reasoning. For foundation-model training, the broader lesson is that the structure of the post-training signal can distort conclusions about model capability.","technical_approach":"The analysis starts from binary-reward GRPO. For a group of G rollouts with rewards r_i∈{+1,-1}, let n+ and n- be the counts of correct and wrong rollouts. GRPO standardizes rewards using the within-group mean and variance. Substituting binary rewards shows that the advantage magnitude is determined by the group composition. In particular, when positives are rare, a positive rollout receives a large positive weight. The estimator cannot tell whether that positive rollout came from reasoning or from chance. The proposed estimator, SignBalance, keeps the verifier sign but replaces the composition-dependent magnitude with a global scale. It then uses stop-gradient per-class rescaling to restore batch-level zero-mean force balance. The PPO-style surrogate is left unchanged, and the method adds no parameters, external model, or inference-time cost.","experiments":"The paper highlights three regimes where the spurious component becomes large. Experiments span math reasoning and search-agent tasks across different model scales, and the reported pattern favors SignBalance over the standard GRPO estimator. It suggests that reasoning gains from OPD are not simply a consequence of imitating the teacher distribution everywhere. A tiny number of high-leverage token updates can be enough to move the model toward better reasoning behavior. This matters for post-training efficiency, but more importantly it changes how OPD should be interpreted. The strongest sparse variants do not necessarily reduce teacher-student reverse KL; some even increase it. That weakens the common explanation that OPD works mainly by distribution matching. For pretraining researchers, the useful lesson is broader: supervision density and supervision quality are separable. Token-level data selection may matter as much as, or more than, the nominal amount of supervised text.","technical_approach":"The method starts from sampled-token OPD. In standard OPD, the student generates on-policy trajectories and receives teacher distribution supervision at each position, which corresponds to minimizing a teacher-student reverse KL objective. The paper keeps the rollout setting fixed and changes only the supervised token subset. It studies random one-token supervision per trajectory and more selective variants that keep tokens with extreme teacher-student probability differences. This selection lets the authors separate positive teacher-preferred tokens from negative teacher-dispreferred tokens and inspect their effects under different teacher-student scale regimes. The key distinction from RLVR is that these token signals are local teacher preferences, not outcome-level credit assignment. The key distinction from dense OPD is that almost all token-level imitation targets are deliberately discarded.","experiments":"$87","reading_guide":"Read the objective and token-selection sections carefully. anchor）θ_n 与当前更新后 checkpoint θ'_{n+1} 的位移 Δ = φ(π_{θ'_{n+1}}) − φ(π_{θ_n}) 作为“近期改进方向”，然后做外推：φ(teacher) = φ(π_{θ'_{n+1}}) + (β−1)·Δ，其中 β>1 表示向前投影到“未来更好”的教师；β=1 退化为无信号（teacher=student）。\n\n两种实例化：\n1) Olympiad 数学题正确率为 52%。把 reviewer 换成跨家族中等模型后，最终正确率提升到 64%，提升 12 个百分点，统计显著性给到 p=0.0005，而且没有出现把正确答案改坏的案例。这个结果说明 reviewer 不需要自己具备完整解题能力，也能通过较好的 rejection targeting 带来净收益。\n\nself-review 的现象更有意思。它的 detection rate 最高，但最终准确率没有显著提升。文中给出的细节是：它的 reject 次数约为有效中等 reviewer 的 2.1 倍，但修好的错误答案只有后者的约三分之一；同时，它会错误拒绝自己 35% 的正确答案。更关键的是，在这些 false rejection 里，只要 executor 真的按 critique 去改，结果都会变错；那些没有造成最终伤害的样本，只是因为 executor 忽略了 critique。作者据此指出，表面上的“低 damage”是 revision conservatism 造成的假象。\n\n最弱 reviewer 基本处于 inert 状态：100 道题里没有改变任何最终答案，但 token 成本大约翻倍。这给出了一个很实用的 capability floor：低于某个能力阈值，review 阶段既不能修错，也不能稳定触发有用修订，只会增加开销。\n\n从实验设置看，作者还处理了一个实现细节：初始运行中发现中等 reviewer 的输出被截断，后续修正了 token limit 并在仓库中记录各模型输出上限。这类细节对复现实验很重要，因为 reviewer 任务依赖完整 critique，截断会直接影响 reject 质量。","reading_guide":"泛读时先看 ta","starred":false,"priority":"p2","reading_tier":"must_read","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"2026-09-05T03:04:23Z","category_id":"post_train","cover_url":"/covers/2609_05837.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.AI"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇工作解决的是一个很现实的 policy，而且不依赖人工标注或外部奖励。论文的关键判断是，失败轨迹并不等于无用轨迹；一条轨迹即便没完成原始意图，也往往完成了某个别的、可描述的子任务，其中包含可复用的动作监督信号。","importance":"这篇对 pretrain 本身不是直接贡献，但对 pretrain ↔ post-train 接口很有价值，尤其是 environment-specific agent adaptation、offline policy learning、以及如何从无标签交互数据中提炼训练信号。它代表了一类越来越重要的训练范式：不再假设有干净任务集和 verifier，而是把真实世界日志当作原料，先重建任务，再做细粒度 credit assignment。对基座研究员来说，启发主要有三点。第一，训练信号可以从行为轨迹内部自举出来，而不是完全依赖外部 reward。第二，trajectory-level filtering 很浪费数据，动作级加权更适合低成功率、长轨迹环境。第三，这种“先解释数据实际完成了什么，再决定怎么学”的思路，与预训练里的数据重标注、合成监督、latent task inference 有相通之处。","technical_approach":"AgentBrew 分三步。第一步是一次性离线数据采集。agent 在真实环境里探索 live state，并提出 grounded tasks，然后执行这些任务，得到一批不做质量过滤的原始轨迹。这里作者刻意不依赖预定义 benchmark task，也不在采集后只保留成功样本，因为真实应用里成功率低、交互昂贵，丢数据代价太高。\n\n第二步是 retrospective task inference。给定一条轨迹，模型不再把原始 instruction 当成唯一监督，而是根据轨迹中的动作序列、工具调用、环境状态变化和最终结果，反推出“这条轨迹实际上完成了什么任务”。这样得到的是对齐后的 instruction–trajectory pair。这个设计解决了一个核心错配：原始任务可能失败，但轨迹中仍然包含对另一个可描述任务的有效执行过程。如果继续拿原始 instruction 监督，模型会学到错误映射；如果直接丢弃，又损失大量可用信号。回溯式任务推断相当于先把标签修正到与行为一致。\n\n第三步是 PMI-based credit assignment。作者把整条轨迹对推断任务 I 的信息量写成 pointwise mutual information，并利用 PMI 的链式分解，把 trajectory-level 信息拆成每一步动作的增量贡献。直观上，某个 action 如果显著提高了“从这条轨迹看出任务 I 已被完成”的概率，它就应获得更高 credit；反之，冗余、无效、偏离目标的动作权重应被压低。训练时，这些 per-action credits 作为 sample weights 进入 policy optimization，放大有信息动作的梯度，抑制噪声动作。相比 rejection sampling 或 trajectory-level filtering，这种做法保留了失败轨迹中的局部有效片段，也避免把整条长轨迹一刀切地判成好或坏。\n\n从方法定位看，它不是在线 RL，也不是纯 SFT。更像一种离线 agent policy learning：先从原始交互中恢复隐含任务结构，再做动作级别的加权行为克隆。与需要 verifier 的成功轨迹蒸馏不同，它把“监督信号从哪里来”这个问题前置解决了。","experiments":"实验在三个真实 MCP 应用上做：GitHub、Notion、PostgreSQL。作者强调这些都是真实、状态化、工具复杂的环境，而不是模拟器。结果上，AgentBrew 在平均指标上相对 Qwen3-32B base 提升 +8.7 Acc 和 +9.7 Score，并且超过更大的 Qwen3-235B；相对 rejection sampling 提升 +5.9 Acc 和 +10.3 Score。这个结果说明，数据利用方式比单纯增大模型规模更关键，尤其在环境特定工具学习里更明显。\n\n从全文给出的论证看，实验重点不只是主结果，还包括两类机制验证。其一，retrospective task inference 是否真的把失败轨迹变成了可学样本。作者通过人工或自动分析展示，很多原始失败轨迹在重标注后变成了与行为一致的训练对。其二，PMI credit 是否优于均匀加权或轨迹级筛选。消融表明，去掉动作级 credit assignment 后，性能会明显回落，说明收益来自更细粒度的监督，而不是单纯多看了数据。\n\n另一个值得注意的点是，作者把方法放在“单批次离线学习”设定下评估，也就是采集结束后不再与环境交互。这一点很关键，因为它排除了 on-policy improvement 带来的额外收益，证明方法确实能从静态日志中提炼出足够强的训练信号。若从工业可用性看，这比依赖大量在线 rollouts 或高保真 simulator 的方案更贴近真实部署条件。","reading_guide":"这篇建议精读。先看 Introduction 和 Problem Formulation，把设定吃透：真实 API 环境、无 verifier、无 simulator、单批次离线数据。然后重点读方法部分的两个核心模块。第一是 retrospective task inference，关注作者如何从轨迹反推 These offsets can dominate token-level update directions and drown out the part of the signal that reflects the teacher’s capability improvement. This matters for distilling from heterogeneous open or closed models, especially when the supervision is dense and likelihood-based.","technical_approach":"The authors decompose the cross-family OPD signal into two terms: a cross-family offset between a weak reference model from the teacher family and the student, and a within-family likelihood shift from that weak reference to the strong teacher. On the student side, a frozen copy of the initial student policy is used as an anchor, so the update is modulated by how far the current student has moved from its initialization. It asks a sharper one: when a model keeps choosing the same answer, is that a stable preference that survives semantic reframing, or merely a wording-sensitive artifact of one prompt form? The authors call the former Deep bias and the latter Shallow bias. This distinction matters because prompt-level concentration alone cannot tell whether a behavior is rooted in pretraining, introduced by post-training, or simply elicited by a brittle surface form.","importance":"Its value for pretraining research is fairly concrete. First, it offers a decomposition of bias that aligns better with training provenance. Biases that survive reframing are much more likely to already exist in the pretrained checkpoint and to persist through SFT, DPO, and RLVR. Biases that disappear under reframing look more like post-training-shaped response habits.
